summary.en: Alvin Hellerstein, the 92‑year-old federal judge who oversaw the Maduro drug-trafficking case, has died, leaving the trial without a presiding judge. A soldier who allegedly bet $400,000 on Maduro’s removal was arrested by the DOJ, and a separate soldier faces a Polymarket insider-trading case. Explosive attacks near the Colombia-Venezuela border injured at least four police officers in one blast and six people, including four officers, in another. Nicolás Maduro is returning to federal court to face torture allegations. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2007.
summary.nb: Alvin Hellerstein, den 92‑årige føderale dommeren som ledet Maduro-saken om narkotikasmugling, er død, og etterlater rettssaken uten en presiderende dommer. En soldat som angivelig skal ha satset 400 000 dollar på Maduros avsettelse, ble arrestert av DOJ, og en annen soldat står overfor en Polymarket-sak om innsidehandel. Eksplosive angrep nær grensen mellom Colombia og Venezuela såret minst fire politibetjenter i ett sprengningsutslag og seks personer, inkludert fire betjenter, i et annet. Nicolás Maduro vender tilbake til føderal domstol for å møte anklager om tortur. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2007.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
